name: Palace of Westminster

position.source: https://www.openstreetmap.org/relation/1567699 (centroid of the relation; smallest rectangle 273.2 × 102.4 m with its long axis at 7.1°, so the river front faces 97.1°)

rights.note: Rebuilt after the fire of 1834 to Sir Charles Barry's design with Augustus Pugin's Gothic Revival detail (1840–1870; the Elizabeth Tower finished in 1859, the Victoria Tower in 1860), completed by Barry's sons Edward Middleton Barry and Charles Barry Jr. (Wikidata lists Charles Barry Jr. among the architects). Westminster Hall is medieval (1097–1099, roof 1393–1401). Every author died before 1945. The Commons chamber was rebuilt after 1945 (Giles Gilbert Scott) inside the old walls; it does not show from outside at this scale.

notes: Built by code (model_sources/Q62408_palace_of_westminster.py, tools/meshkit.py) with AI assistance. Filed under the Palace of Westminster (Q62408); the Elizabeth Tower, Big Ben (Q41225), and the Victoria Tower (Q1858077) are part of the model. Heading 97.1°: the river (east) front on the Thames is the main façade (+Z), so the Victoria Tower stands at the −X (south) end and the Elizabeth Tower at the +X (north) end. Massing from the OpenStreetMap building:parts: every part at its OSM height with its roof shape (gabled, hipped, mansard, skillion, pyramidal, flat); dark cast-iron roofs with iron cresting, lead flats, sandy-grey Anston limestone. The Perpendicular bays (buttress shafts rising as small pinnacles above the parapet, rows of mullioned windows, string courses) are generated on every wall that OSM shows exposed — a stylised rhythm, not the real window count. Small turret parts become octagonal pinnacles. The three great towers are built by hand: the Victoria Tower (OSM stages scaled to the published 98.5 m, corner turrets, the Sovereign's Entrance arch on its south and west faces, the flagstaff to 120 m as in OSM with the Union Flag), the Elizabeth Tower (12.2 m shaft, clock stage with four 7 m dials centred 55 m up, gilded frames and hands, the belfry, the cast-iron spire with lucarnes and gilded ribs, the Ayrton light, finial at 96 m) and the Central Tower (octagonal lantern and stone spire raised to the published 91 m; OSM stops at 78 m). Westminster Hall from its OSM parts with the great north window; the river terrace (OSM way 367645111) with its parapet and the river wall down to y = −6 m. Uncertain: the stages of the Elizabeth Tower spire above 61 m (from photos, ±5 %), the exact shape of the Victoria Tower top and the height of its flagstaff (OSM 120 m, ±10 %), whether the Sovereign's Entrance arch also opens on the west face, the rhythm and number of the windows, the roofs that OSM tags only roughly. Not included: Westminster Abbey, Westminster Bridge, Portcullis House, New and Old Palace Yard, Speaker's Green and Black Rod's Garden. footprint: the palace, Westminster Hall, the towers and the terrace (courtyards included), +1 m.
